title: Restore chat state when resuming client sessions

observation: Development work should favor TDD, simple solutions, and pausing only when blocked by missing specifications or external issues.
Code changes should keep functions focused, names intention-revealing, and tests self-validating.
Use structured worklog tools as the source of truth; add tasks before implementation, update task state, and record validation observations.

The mobile app opens or reopens Pi sessions from saved host/path/session combinations and should show live timeline state in the session view; tests include shared reducer/protocol, host API, and mobile view-model transitions.
Useful validation commands are `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and package-filtered variants; root scripts build shared before recursive typecheck/test.

title: Research session resume flow, host snapshot behavior, and existing tests
Add failing coverage for restoring chat timeline/state when reopening a persisted session
Implement chat state restoration for resumed sessions
Run focused validation and record results

content: Starting codebase research to identify how the client opens previous sessions and where chat/timeline state should be restored.

observation: Open previous connects to the saved host, resolves the saved session file if needed, POSTs openSession({cwd, sessionFile, mode:'open'}), dispatches a session_opened host event with the returned snapshot, and the SessionScreen renders snapshot.timeline. The client is already wired to use snapshot timeline state.

SdkSessionRunner snapshots include only the in-memory timeline array built from live SDK events after the runner starts. createState reads session.messages.length, but no timeline items are reconstructed from session.messages when opening a persisted session.
Opening a prior session goes through SessionManager.open(sessionFile, undefined, cwd), so the SDK session should expose prior AgentSession.messages after runtime creation.

Live timeline projection handles assistant/thinking text deltas and tool execution start/update/end events. Timeline ids generated during live streaming use assistant-*, thinking-*, tool-*, and recordUserMessage uses user-* ids, so restored history should avoid those prefixes to prevent collisions with future live events.
AgentSession exposes messages as AgentMessage[], including user, assistant, and toolResult LLM messages plus custom Pi messages.

Persisted message shapes include user content as string or text/image blocks, assistant content as text/thinking/toolCall blocks, and toolResult messages with toolCallId, toolName, content, details, isError, and timestamp.

Pi TUI restores session chat by rendering SessionManager.buildSessionContext(): user messages, assistant messages, assistant tool calls, and subsequent toolResult messages matched back to pending tool components.

content: Research found the bug is on the host snapshot side: the mobile client renders snapshot.timeline when opening previous sessions, but SdkSessionRunner only fills timeline from live events and does not derive timeline items from existing SDK session.messages.
